body:
> I want to be able to map the exceptions to what I want, without having to register a Vert.x route just to be able to override the QuarkusHttpUser.AUTH_FAILURE_HANDLER, and I'd prefer if it were mapped by RESTEasy Reactive using the existing exception mapping process.

Sounds totally legit to me

Greetings team,

Any news on this matter? If not, is there a sane workaround?

I'd like to be able to throw exceptions in `HttpAuthenticationMechanism` and catch them uniformly with what RR has to offer, but the problem is similar: exception is ignored. For now I've come up with smth like propagating "dummy" headers bearing error data from my `HttpAuthenticationMechanism` implementation all the way to a `@ServerResponseFilter` at the end, where I basically rewrite the entire response, but this feels a bit too hacky.

Also, a fun point: apparently, whatever headers I set to `HttpServerResponse` via `RoutingContext` available in `HttpAuthenticationMechanism#authenticate`, they are not synced with `ContainerResponseContext`, which is evident in the `@ServerResponseMapper`. I guess it may make sense, but still feels sort of weird that 2 _similar_ objects bear different sets of headers at the end.
@michalvavrik This issue may have been fixed as well by your PR

@sberyozkin this issue covers all the cases when default auth failure handlers ends response. Let me create PR, I think there is an easy solution that covers both issues you have commented me in. I had it in my PR, but we agreed to handle it separately.

issue.title: Let RESTEasy Reactive exception mappers handle authentication failure with disabled proactive security
issue.body:
fixes: #25732
fixes:  #22971
fixes: #26314 (for proactive=false)

There are situations (e.g. permissions check, see #22971) when authentication is performed before RESTEasy Reactive begin processing, thus simply removing default authentication failure handler won't do. Users expects that exceptions mappers are going to be invoked (which is not a case).

This PR provides it's own auth failure handler that fails the event and let RR abort handlers to deal with exceptions. It intentionally handles only `proactive=false` scenarios (still, it fixes linked issues). It's necessary to differ between situations when RR begun procession (then we shouldn't fail event as it would be handled by both failure handlers and abort handlers) and didn't begin processing. I added `ExceptionMapperTest`, IT version can't be added as it requires disabled proactive security (build time property, so test profile won't do), we don't have suitable module for this.
